title.source: How does changing scale change the story?

read.sections.0.text.source: On a map on a screen, you can zoom in to see one street or zoom out to see a whole country. Historians do something similar with the past, because they choose a scale. Scale means how big a piece of time, place or group you decide to study. A close scale looks at one day, one letter or one family. A wide scale might follow a whole town for 100 years, or compare many regions over thousands of years. Look at Riverstone. At the scale of one afternoon, the story is about rain and a closed bridge. Over 20 years, it is about a town that grows. Over several hundred years, it is about a river that moves.
read.sections.0.text.back: On a map on a screen, you can zoom in to see one street or zoom out to see a whole country. Historians do something similar with the past, because they choose a scale. Scale means the size of the stretch of time, place or group of people you choose to study. A close scale looks at one day, one letter or one family. A wide scale might follow a whole town over 100 years, or compare many regions over thousands of years. Look at the town of Riverstone. Seen at the scale of one afternoon, the story is rain and a closed bridge. Seen over 20 years, the story is a growing town. Seen over several hundred years, the story is a river that moves.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: On a map, you can zoom in and out. Historians do this with the past too. They choose a scale. Scale means how much time or place you look at. A close scale is one day or one family. A wide scale is a town over 100 years. In Riverstone, the story of one afternoon is about rain and a bridge. Over 20 years, the town grows. Over hundreds of years, the river moves.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: On a map, you can zoom in and zoom out. Historians do this with the past too. They choose a scale. Scale means how much time or place we look at. A close scale is one day or one family. A wide scale is one town over 100 years. In Riverstone, the story of one afternoon is rain and a bridge. Over 20 years, the town grows. Over several hundred years, the river moves.

read.sections.1.text.source: A close view helps us notice people's choices, feelings and small details. A diary, a receipt or one photograph can show how an event changed one person's day. For example, a trader's diary might say that she waited six hours for the bridge to open. However, one person's day is not always the same as everyone else's. Other traders may have taken the long road instead. So close evidence needs context, which means we need to know what was happening around it at the time.
read.sections.1.text.back: A close view helps us notice people's decisions, feelings and small details. One diary, receipt or photo can show how an event changed one person's day. For example, a trader's diary might say she waited six hours for the bridge to open. But one person's day is not always the same as other people's days. Other traders may have used a longer road instead. So close-up evidence needs context, which means we need to know what was happening around that evidence at the time.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: A close view shows people. We see their choices and feelings. A diary or a receipt shows one person's day. A trader may wait six hours for the bridge. But other traders may take the long road. One person's day is not everyone's day. So we need context. Context is what is going on around the source.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: A close view shows people. We see their decisions and feelings. A diary or a receipt shows one person's day. One trader may have waited six hours for the bridge. But others may have used a longer road. One person's day is not everyone's day. So we need context. Context is what happens around a source.

read.sections.2.text.note: "universe" is จักรวาล (everyday word) here and in L04; Thai science classes use เอกภพ. Check which the course should use.
read.sections.2.text.source: A wide view helps us see a pattern, which is a change that repeats or goes on for a long time. Maps from many different years can show Riverstone slowly spreading across the river. But a wide view can also hide people, because a line on a timeline cannot show every person's choices. Some historians zoom out as far as possible, to the whole history of the universe. At that scale, one town is far too small to see. That is why historians move between scales. Neither scale is always better, because the best scale depends on the question you ask.
read.sections.2.text.back: A wide view helps us see patterns, which are changes that repeat or go on for a long time. Maps from many different years show that Riverstone slowly spread across the river. But a wide view can also hide people, because a line on a timeline cannot show everyone's decisions. Some historians zoom out as far as they can, to the whole history of the universe. At that scale, one town is too small to see. This is why historians switch back and forth between scales. No scale is always better, because the best scale depends on the question you ask.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: A wide view shows a pattern. A pattern is a change that goes on for a long time. Maps from many years show the town getting bigger. But a wide view can hide people. A timeline cannot show every person. Some historians look at the whole universe. Then you cannot see one town at all. So historians move from close to wide. The best scale depends on your question.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: A wide view shows patterns. A pattern is a change that happens over a long time. Maps from many years show the town getting bigger. But a wide view may hide people. A timeline cannot show everyone. Some historians look at the whole universe. Then you can't see the town at all. So historians change from close to wide. The best scale depends on your question.

write.example.source: At the scale of one afternoon, we notice heavy rain and a closed bridge. A trader has to take a longer road, so she arrives late. Over 20 years, the evidence shows a town that is growing. New homes and markets spread to both sides of the river. The close scale helps us answer why one trader was late that day. The wide scale helps us answer why Riverstone built two new bridges. Together, the two scales show that one place can have more than one story.
write.example.back: At the scale of one afternoon, we notice heavy rain and a closed bridge. One trader had to use a longer road, so she arrived late. Over 20 years, the evidence shows the town was growing. New homes and markets spread out on both sides of the river. The close scale helps us answer why one trader arrived late that day. The wide scale helps us answer why Riverstone built two new bridges. Looking at both scales together shows that one place can have more than one story.

watch.summary.note: "13.8 billion" is written 13.8 พันล้านปี so the digits match the English; 13,800 ล้านปี is the more usual Thai form. Same in L04.
watch.summary.source: This short video uses the widest scale there is: the history of the whole universe. Scientists explain that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago. At first, it was very small and very hot. Then it grew bigger and cooler. It has kept changing ever since. At this scale, you do not see any person, town or country. You see only very big changes over billions of years. This helps us see that human history is a small part of a much longer story. But this scale cannot tell us why one trader was late, or how one family lived. To learn those things, historians zoom in.
watch.summary.back: This short video uses the widest scale there is: the history of the whole universe. Scientists explain that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago. At first it was very small and very hot, then it grew bigger and cooled down, and it has kept changing ever since. At this scale you don't see any people, towns or countries. You see only very large changes over billions of years. This helps us see that human history is just a small part of a much longer story. But this scale can't tell why one trader arrived late, or how one family lived. To know these things, historians must zoom in.
